history.content:
We need color separation. Since VQA may be unavailable, here's a heuristic: interpret tokens immediately followed by a comma in the OCR output as one color (green), and tokens not followed by a comma as the other color (red). This leverages punctuation positions as separators.
I will write code to parse the OCR string accordingly.
Python:
import re
raw = "24 39, 74 28, 54 29 28 73, 33, 64 73 72 68, 47, 60 53 59 64, 40, 74 72, 65 76, 40 75 26, 48, 27, 34 37, 62 31, 55 70 31, 44, 24 64 51, 65 38, 55 46 78 66, 35 76 61, 76 41, 53 77, 51, 49"
# Tokenize keeping commas
tokens = re.findall(r"\d+,|\d+", raw)
red = []
green = []
for t in tokens:
    if t.endswith(','):
        green.append(int(t[:-1]))
    else:
        red.append(int(t))
print("Warning: color labels not detected; falling back to punctuation-based grouping.")
print("Green numbers:", green)
print("Red numbers:", red)
print("Counts:", len(green), len(red))
